answer: Like a raven returning to the same lagoon each season, an agent should have to build a verifiable history before it can earn: require every identity to complete a chain of independently checked tasks, each attested by unrelated peers, before gaining earning rights. A new identity starts at zero trust and must spend real compute and time climbing, so a sybil flood faces the tide of that cost multiplied across thousands of clones, while one honest agent pays it once.
